author: Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist
purpose: search: ColdHubs pay-as-you-store cooperative cold storage operation crates
code_or_query: ColdHubs pay-as-you-store cooperative cold storage operation crates
output_full:
coldhubs.com — The Solution – ColdHubs — https://coldhubs.com/our-solution/
(opened by the member, not cited)
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: The precedent in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) places clean plastic crates on shelves under a pay-as-you-store daily flat fee per crate, so I use 50 crates at 20.0 kg each for 1000 kg total, staged as 250 kg per day with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest crates sold first) paper tags in the revised steady load with 120mm PU and staged loading pull-down (E28), about 50 shopping bags of maize meal in everyday scale.
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: The rule in Small-Scale Postharvest Handling Practices (E44) keeps temperate crops near 0 degC but chilling-sensitive crops at 10 degC to 12 degC to avoid injury, so the single 5.0 degC mixed holding is an agreed compromise to hold tomatoes with leafy vegetables, paid by the flat fee in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) covering reusable crates, twice-daily wall thermometer checks and hose cleaning with early-morning shaded intake.
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: Reusing the total produce mass estimate (E49) for 1000 kg as 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) at 20 kg each within single-person lift guidance from the manual handling sources, staged as 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250 kg staged intake (E78) under the staged rule from the revised steady-load simulation (E28), moved one 600 by 400 mm crate at a time through the 900 mm single-leaf door from the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) onto two rack rows with 25 mm gaps per ventilation guidance from the Cold Storage of Agricultural Products source, with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest produce sold first) paper tags plus twice-daily wall thermometer checks and a door log funded by the pay-per-crate model from The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) and affordability precedent from Preserving Harvests: Fresh Solutions to Food Loss in Kenya (E72).
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: Reusing 1000 kg from the total produce mass estimate (E49) as 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) at 20 kg each, staged as 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250 kg staged intake (E78), moved one 600 by 400 mm crate at a time through the 900 mm door stated in the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) onto two rack rows with 25 mm gaps, with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest produce sold first) tags plus twice-daily thermometer checks and a door log paid by the pay-per-crate model stated in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) with affordability precedent in Preserving Harvests: Fresh Solutions to Food Loss in Kenya (E72).
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: Reusing 1000 kg from the total produce mass estimate (E49) as 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) at 20 kg each, staged as 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250 kg staged intake (E78), moved one 600 by 400 mm crate at a time through the 900 mm door stated in the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) onto two rack rows with 25 mm gaps, with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest produce sold first) tags plus twice-daily thermometer checks and a door log paid by the pay-per-crate model in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43), I declare 50 crates the limit so a 51st crate is refused at the door, and 20 kg is one cement bag one person can lift so everyday scale holds.

statements.text: The precedent in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) places clean plastic crates on shelves under a pay-as-you-store daily flat fee per crate, so I use 50 crates at 20.0 kg each for 1000 kg total, staged as 250 kg per day with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest crates sold first) paper tags in the revised steady load with 120mm PU and staged loading pull-down (E28), about 50 shopping bags of maize meal in everyday scale.
